question: What is the difference between compile-time and runtime polymorphism?

scenes.sub: Same goal, different moment: the compiler decides, or the running program does.
scenes.say: Compile time versus runtime polymorphism. Both let one piece of code work with many types. The difference is when the decision is made.

scenes.head: The same idea, written both ways

panels.label: compile time
runtime

scenes.say: On the left, a template. Dog and Cat don't share any base class. The compiler generates a separate talk for Dog and for Cat, and each call is wired directly to the right speak. On the right, a single talk function takes any Animal by reference. Which speak runs is decided while the program is running, through the virtual function.

scenes.head: When the type is only known at runtime
scenes.say: Here runtime polymorphism is essential. The type depends on user input, so the compiler can't know it. In practice, each object carries a hidden pointer to its class's virtual table. The call follows pet to the object, then to its table, then to Dog's speak. That's an extra indirection, and it usually prevents inlining. A template can't do this, because templates need the type at compile time.

scenes.head: Side by side
rows: Types must be known at compile time
Type can be chosen at runtime
Small overhead, needs pointers or references
scenes.say: Compile time is decided by the compiler, runtime while the program runs. The mechanism: overloading and templates, versus virtual functions through a base pointer or reference. They're also called static and dynamic binding. Call cost: a direct call that can be inlined, versus an indirect call. Flexibility: types fixed at compile time, versus chosen at runtime. Downsides: code bloat and slower builds, versus a small runtime overhead.

lines: Compile-time: overloads and templates, resolved by the compiler. Fast.
Runtime: virtual functions via base pointer/reference, resolved via vtable.
Use runtime when the type is only known while running; else templates.
scenes.say: Compile time polymorphism is overloads and templates, resolved by the compiler, with no runtime cost. Runtime polymorphism is virtual functions, resolved through the v table. Pick runtime when the type is only known while running.
